/no_think
You are the scope check for MedX, an assistant for psychiatry and mental health based on the DSM-5.

In scope: mental disorders (diagnosis, criteria, symptoms, course, prevalence, risk factors, differential
diagnosis), psychiatric treatment and psychopharmacology, substance use, intoxication and withdrawal, sleep,
eating, neurocognitive and neurodevelopmental disorders, personality, psychotherapy, suicide and self-harm,
and behavioral science.

Out of scope: questions mainly about another field of medicine (cardiology, pulmonology, infectious disease,
biochemistry, endocrinology, surgery, otology and so on), even when the patient also mentions stress, mood,
anxiety or sleep in passing. Judge what the question is asking, not incidental details of the case.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"in_scope": true or false, "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
Question:
A 20-year-old woman presents with persistent sadness for the last 2 months. She says that she is always feeling tired and nothing seems to cheer her up. Although previously a top student at her college, she did not register for classes this term, because she does not feel like going to school anymore. She says her friends complain that she does not want to ‘hang out’ with them anymore. She is sleeping more than usual and often does not want to leave the bed in the morning. The patient denies any suicidal ideation or preoccupation with death. Her past medical history is unremarkable. She currently takes a daily multivitamin. The vital signs include pulse 64/min, respiratory rate 12/min, blood pressure 110/70 mm Hg, and temperature 36.9°C (98.5°F). Her body mass index (BMI) is 17.5 kg/m2. On physical examination, the patient is pale. Mucous membranes and oral cavity are dry with poor dentition. Multiple calluses are present on the knuckles of her left hand. Which of the following medications is the best course of treatment in this patient?

Options:
A. Trazodone
B. Mirtazapine
C. Lorazepam
D. Bupropion
E. Amitriptyline

text: {"in_scope": true, "reason": "The question asks about pharmacological treatment for depressive symptoms in a young adult, which falls under psychiatric treatment and psychopharmacology."}
